summary:
I checked the top signals on 27 Oct 2026. The best opportunity is new: Vanda's Phase 3 Study 3601 of tradipitant (brand name NEREUS) came out today, 27 Oct (PR Newswire, HCPLive, Fierce Pharma). It's a randomized trial with 306 people. Any vomiting after one semaglutide 1 mg dose given without the usual gradual dose increase was 43.0% on tradipitant versus 58.5% on placebo (p=0.006). Vanda plans an FDA filing, called an sNDA. YouTube coverage is close to zero. It fits our best lanes: side effects, nausea and getting more from GLP-1. There are 2 limits. It's a one-dose challenge study, probably in volunteers rather than people on long-term treatment (to be confirmed). And there are no tirzepatide data. Because of that it's a Lane C long-form only under a relaxed rule: tradipitant is an anti-vomiting add-on, not a next-gen GLP-1 drug. If the Editor-in-Chief says no, it becomes a 13:00 Short.

Second: ACOG's first guidance on GLP-1s in pregnancy (Healio, 23 Oct) hit mainstream news today (NewsNation: "stop 1–2 months before trying for a baby"). It's rising fast, with high search intent and few creators covering it. It suits a calm "honest uncertainty" body-worry Short and possibly a long-form, framed as "talk to your prescriber before trying to conceive".

The Lane A queue in the playbook still holds. This week's journal papers give each video something new to say:
- bones and muscle: the Arch Osteoporos systematic review (23 Oct) and the J Clin Med muscle-mass cohort (15 Oct)
- stopping: the Metabolites weight-regain systematic review (9 Oct) and CBC's "going on and off" feature (27 Oct)
- hair: the Med Sci (Basel) review of skin side effects
- plateau: the J Clin Med Türkiye real-world cohort and the medRxiv care-patterns study

Watch Lilly's Q3 earnings on 29 Oct: any new retatrutide or orforglipron trial data from randomized trials would be a Lane C trigger within 48 hours.

Real-world kidney data from ASN Kidney Week (CKD plus obesity without diabetes: 3.3% versus 6.0% over 5 years, observational, Pharmacy Times 27 Oct) and the UBT251 Cell Metabolism paper (a triple agonist versus semaglutide 1 mg) are good material for Shorts.

Retatrutide for sleep apnea is now peaking (Gizmodo, Medscape and others on 26 Oct). Only use it as a Short that compares it with tirzepatide's sleep apnea trial (SURMOUNT-OSA), clearly framed as separate trials, not head-to-head.

Rejected: the "cheapest compounded tirzepatide online" listicle, and microdosing (still circulating).

candidates.topic: A pill to prevent GLP-1 vomiting? Tradipitant (NEREUS) Phase 3 Study 3601: any vomiting 43.0% (61/142) vs 58.5% (96/164) on placebo after a single 1 mg semaglutide dose given without gradual dose increases (Vanda, Oct 27, 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane C (if the Editor-in-Chief accepts an add-on medicine as a 'named drug') or a 13:00 lead Short. Open on 'you just started your GLP-1 and the nausea hit.' Lead with the new result, and give absolute rates for each group (43.0% vs 58.5%; vomiting plus severe nausea 33.1% vs 50.6%). Explain how an NK-1 blocker works on the brain's vomiting centre. Be honest about the limits: it was a one-dose challenge model with no gradual dose increase, so it doesn't reflect how semaglutide is actually started. There are no tirzepatide data. It isn't approved for this use, and an FDA filing is only planned. Close with what already helps today (eating slowly, smaller meals, stopping before full, hydration, telling your prescriber). Not personal advice; talk to your doctor or prescriber.
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–10 days (investor and trade press today; consumer health sites next)
candidates.why_now: Phase 3 topline was first public on Oct 27, 2026, so it's inside the 48 h Lane C window. It's a randomized trial with a semaglutide arm. Nausea and vomiting are the top worries among GLP-1 users (Everyday Health survey, Oct 27; our nausea Short got 147 on YouTube and 120 on Instagram). Very few creator videos so far.

evidence.signal: Phase 3, n=306; any vomiting 43.0% vs 58.5% (p=0.006); vomiting plus worst nausea score ≥3 33.1% vs 50.6%; semaglutide 1 mg single dose without titration; sNDA planned
Clinical press pickup on the same day
Trial registry: tradipitant after a GLP-1 dose in volunteers who are healthy, overweight or have class I–II obesity. Check that this population matches Study 3601
Earlier Phase 2: 29.3% vs 58.6% vomiting after 1 mg Wegovy

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and pregnancy planning: ACOG's first guidance (Oct 23, 2026) says clinicians should consider stopping GLP-1s 1–2 months before conception. Mainstream pickup today (NewsNation, Oct 27)
candidates.angle: Calm 'honest uncertainty' body-worry Short at 08:00. The core message: safety data in pregnancy are limited, so ACOG advises planning ahead with your prescriber, not stopping on your own. Cover what ACOG says about breastfeeding (monitor infant weight; avoid while nursing preterm babies and newborns). Add the reassuring July 2026 data showing no detectable increase in risk after exposure around conception, using 'linked to' wording. Quote ACOG's own words, dated. Include 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own', 'not personal advice' and the prescriber line. Avoid dosing details.
candidates.why_now: Guidance first came out Oct 23 (Healio, Becker's) and crossed into mainstream news Oct 27. Women of reproductive age are a large, fast-growing GLP-1 group, and health creators have barely covered the guidance.

evidence.signal: ACOG issues long-awaited guidance; consider stopping 1–2 months before conception
GLP-1s may be an option while nursing, with monitoring
New research on early-pregnancy exposure eases fears

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your bones and muscle: Arch Osteoporos systematic review of skeletal effects (Oct 23, 2026) plus J Clin Med study of weight-loss size, fat mass and device-estimated muscle loss (Oct 15)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form test, per the playbook. Open on 'you're losing weight on tirzepatide, so is some of it bone and muscle?' Answer within 15 s: part of the weight lost is lean mass, and trials and reviews show what helps (protein, resistance training). Use the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy, the new bone review and the device-measured muscle cohort. State each population clearly. Re-hook roughly every minute.
keywords: how to keep muscle on tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; refreshed by the Oct 23 review (2–4 weeks)
candidates.why_now: Fresh systematic review (Oct 23) and a muscle cohort (Oct 15). Our own bones Short (235) and muscle Short (133) were top performers. This topic has appeared in 9 of our snapshots, scoring 68–72 each time.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of skeletal effects in adults with overweight or obesity
Weight-loss size, fat mass and device-estimated muscle loss during obesity medicine

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 plus the new Metabolites systematic review of weight regain after GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 drugs (Oct 9) and CBC's 'Everyone's going on and off GLP-1s' (Oct 27)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. Open on 'you're thinking about stopping, so what actually happens?' Answer first: weight tends to come back for many people. SURMOUNT-4: 335 vs 335 people randomized at week 36, and the +14.0% regain was measured from week 36 to week 88. Add what the review says about blood sugar and blood pressure drifting back. End with questions to plan with your prescriber. Say clearly: 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own.'
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; the CBC feature adds mainstream interest this week
candidates.why_now: Mainstream on/off coverage today (CBC). A systematic review is the fresh hook. 6 or more snapshots at 70. Third in the playbook's Lane A order.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of weight regain after stopping GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 drugs
'Everyone's going on — and off — GLP-1s'
Randomized Phase 2b: how long semaglutide's effects last after stopping (HIV lipohypertrophy; a niche population)

candidates.topic: Protein on tirzepatide: how much and why, refreshed by the muscle-loss cohort (J Clin Med, Oct 15) and the 'NAD+ booster to protect muscle' hype (Longevity.Technology, Oct 27)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. Open on 'you can barely finish a meal, so how do you get enough protein?' Cover protein targets as guideline ranges for adults on weight-loss treatment (no drug dosing), easy high-protein foods for small appetites, and why supplements like NAD+ boosters don't have human evidence for protecting muscle on GLP-1s. Include 'not personal advice' and the prescriber or dietitian line.
candidates.why_now: Second in the playbook's Lane A order. New muscle-loss data plus booster hype gives a correction angle. Holiday-eating season is starting.

evidence.signal: Muscle and fat mass changes during obesity medicine
Booster-hype hook for a myth-correction section

candidates.topic: Lilly Q3 earnings (Oct 29, 2026): watch for new retatrutide or orforglipron trial data
candidates.angle: Watch item, not a topic yet. If Lilly releases a new randomized result with a headline efficacy number on Oct 29, make it the Lane C long-form within 48 h, drug name first. If it's only filing or timing news (e.g. a retatrutide FDA filing in Q1 2027), make it a retatrutide 'what's confirmed?' Short with a loop ending instead.
candidates.why_now: Earnings are confirmed for Oct 29. Retatrutide has given us our highest Short peaks (262, 199). More Phase 3 retatrutide results are expected over the coming year.

evidence.signal: Lilly Q3 2026 earnings preview
Third Phase 3 win for retatrutide

candidates.topic: Retatrutide versus tirzepatide for sleep apnea: TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA (NEJM) versus SURMOUNT-OSA, now in mainstream news (Gizmodo, Medscape, Oct 26)
candidates.angle: 13:00 two-drug Short with tirzepatide named first. Tirzepatide is approved for sleep apnea with obesity; retatrutide is investigational. Give the drop in breathing interruptions per hour in each trial, with its population (TRIUMPH: BMI 27+, 243 adults without diabetes and 448 with type 2 diabetes). Say 'separate trials, not head-to-head' and list common side effects for both drugs. Use a loop ending.
candidates.why_now: Mainstream wave on Oct 26 (Gizmodo, Medscape, NewsBytes). We cover it with a differentiated head-to-head framing, never a bare repeat.

evidence.signal: 'The Most Powerful Obesity Drug Yet Has a Hidden Benefit'
Review of tirzepatide sleep apnea trial evidence

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and kidneys in people without diabetes: ASN Kidney Week 2026 real-world study (CKD plus obesity, 5-year kidney failure composite 3.3% vs 6.0%), plus FLOW safety by CKD stage (Kidney Int, Oct 20)
candidates.angle: Short (benefits-beyond-weight pillar). Use 'linked to' language because it's observational. Name all the drugs in the cohort, including tirzepatide. Contrast with FLOW's randomized evidence, which is in type 2 diabetes plus CKD with semaglutide 1 mg. Never put 'kidney failure' alone on a caption card.
candidates.why_now: Pharmacy Times pickup on Oct 27 from ASN Kidney Week, the FLOW safety paper on Oct 20, and retatrutide's TRANSCEND-CKD trial in the same week. Several independent sources.

evidence.signal: 3.3% vs 6.0% 5-year composite kidney outcome; CKD plus obesity without diabetes; observational
FLOW safety outcomes by CKD severity

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common is it and what helps? (Med Sci (Basel) systematic review of skin side effects, Oct 9; July 2026 matched cohort)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 4th in queue. Open on 'your hairbrush looks fuller than usual.' Answer first: it's usually temporary shedding linked to rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium). Give trial rates for tirzepatide versus placebo, then explain what helps (protein, iron and checks with your doctor). Observational relative risks get 'linked to' wording.
keywords: does hair grow back after Ozempic
candidates.why_now: New systematic review; a top search-intent body worry; ranked 4th in the playbook's Lane A order.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of skin side effects with semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide weight-loss plateau: what the trials and new real-world data show (J Clin Med Türkiye cohort, Oct 13; medRxiv care patterns after starting treatment, Oct 6)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 5th in queue (note: L2 10-27 already shipped a plateau video, so use this as a Short or a refresh only after it's scored at day 7). The new hook: the medRxiv study links follow-up care after starting treatment to weight loss in everyday practice (observational).
keywords: why did I stop losing weight on GLP-1
candidates.why_now: New real-world data; high-intent search. Avoid duplicating the 10-27 long-form.

evidence.signal: Care patterns after starting treatment and weight loss with semaglutide and tirzepatide
Real-world weight trajectories with semaglutide and tirzepatide (Türkiye)

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving and holiday meals on tirzepatide or semaglutide: protein first, smaller plates, eating slowly, easing fullness (Channel 3000, Oct 27; UC Davis guide)
candidates.angle: Body-worry or practical Short now. Consider a Lane A long-form around Nov 10–18 ('Tirzepatide and Thanksgiving: What Helps With Fullness and Nausea'). Include the tradipitant news as a 'what's coming' aside only once it's verified. No extreme-diet messaging.
candidates.why_now: Seasonal cycle starting (local TV pickup on Oct 27); has appeared in 4 or more snapshots at 70–73. Search demand will rise over the next 3 weeks.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1 use during the holidays'

candidates.topic: UBT251 (a GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist licensed by Novo, sometimes called 'Novo's answer to retatrutide') versus semaglutide 1 mg in type 2 diabetes: Phase 2 published in Cell Metabolism (Oct 26). HbA1c −2.16 vs −1.77 points; weight up to −9.8% vs −4.8% at 24 weeks
candidates.angle: 13:00 head-to-head Short. Name semaglutide 1 mg as the trial's comparator, and say it's Phase 2, Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, starting HbA1c 8.12%, 24 weeks. Not Lane C, because topline results were first public in March 2026.
candidates.why_now: Peer-reviewed publication on Oct 26 plus Inside Precision Medicine pickup. A randomized arm against semaglutide.

evidence.signal: Multicenter randomized Phase 2 in type 2 diabetes
HbA1c −2.16 vs −1.77 (semaglutide 1 mg) vs −0.66 (placebo); weight up to −9.8% vs −4.8%

candidates.topic: 'GLP-1 companion' supplements and boosters: the industry itself warns of an evidence gap (Nutrition Insight, Oct 27), on top of Reuters/Fortune coverage. What fibre, protein and eating order really do to your own GLP-1
candidates.angle: Short in the myths pillar: what's confirmed versus what's marketing. Supplements don't replace the medicine. Food-based effects on your own GLP-1 are real but modest. No brand or product names.
candidates.why_now: A fourth independent source this week. Seen in 4 snapshots at 62–68.

evidence.signal: Suppliers warn the GLP-1 companion category risks a credibility gap without evidence

candidates.topic: Running, marathons and exercise on GLP-1s: fueling, nausea and slower stomach emptying (The Guardian, Oct 27)
candidates.angle: Body-worry Short. Explain why slower stomach emptying can make race-day fuel and big efforts feel rough, and why strength training matters more for keeping muscle. Point to the Strength Training on Tirzepatide video as the funnel. No fueling or dosing protocols; talk to your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Guardian personal story out today. Mainstream sports coverage has only just started.

evidence.signal: ''I was so sick': is running a marathon while on a GLP-1 a bad idea?'

candidates.topic: GLP-1s for weight gain from antipsychotic medicines: new systematic review and meta-analysis (Eur J Clin Pharmacol, Oct 24), plus a MedPage case report on possible psychiatric-medication interactions (Oct 26)
candidates.angle: Short in the 'who it may help' pillar. Report what the meta-analysis found for weight and metabolic markers, and stress coordinating with both prescribers. Never suggest changing psychiatric medicines; frame the case report as a single case.
candidates.why_now: A fresh meta-analysis of randomized trials; an underserved audience; almost no creator coverage.

evidence.signal: Systematic review and meta-analysis of GLP-1s for overweight and metabolic problems caused by antipsychotics

candidates.topic: Gray-market GLP-1 crackdown: an online platform agrees to stop selling GLP-1 drugs to US customers (ABC News, Oct 27), plus the nationwide recall of compounded tirzepatide vials from a Cary, North Carolina compounder (Oct 26)
candidates.angle: The week's one gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Short. Stick to dated official facts only, never name a seller or buying route, and close with 'get GLP-1s only through a licensed prescriber and pharmacy.' Low priority on Instagram, where this genre gets 0–30 reach.
candidates.why_now: Two dated enforcement facts within 24 h.
